israel-lebanon-strikes-2026.title: Israeli Military Campaign in Lebanon (2026)
israel-lebanon-strikes-2026.summary: Israel's sustained air and ground campaign against Hezbollah in southern Lebanon, ongoing since 2 March 2026, producing mounting civilian casualties, repeated incidents involving UNIFIL peacekeepers, and a security zone approximately 10 km inside Lebanese territory. Israel broke the ceasefire announced on 19 June 2026 the following day, killing at least 50 people and triggering Iran's reclosure of the Strait of Hormuz.

us-iran-mou-2026.title: US-Iran Memorandum of Understanding and Implementation Crisis
us-iran-mou-2026.summary: The Memorandum of Understanding signed by Presidents Trump and Pezeshkian in mid-June 2026 ended the active US military phase of the US-Iran conflict that began in late February 2026. Its terms included lifting the US naval blockade, reopening the Strait of Hormuz, and a 60-day ceasefire window. Israel's refusal to end its Lebanon offensive placed the MoU in immediate jeopardy; Iran reclosed the Strait of Hormuz on 20 June citing Israeli breaches. Israeli public opinion turned sharply against Trump, with 71 percent no longer trusting the administration.

icc-israel-warrants-2026.title: ICC Proceedings Against Israeli Officials
icc-israel-warrants-2026.summary: International Criminal Court proceedings against Israeli officials that escalated in 2025–2026. Following arrest warrants for Prime Minister Netanyahu and former Defense Minister Gallant in November 2024, the ICC prosecutor requested a warrant for Finance Minister Smotrich in May 2026, citing forced displacement orders, support for settler expansion into occupied territory, and his public statement that starving Palestinians may be 'justified and moral.' Smotrich responded by announcing he would sign an evacuation order for the Bedouin community of Khan al-Ahmar.

gaza-territorial-control-2026.title: Israeli Territorial Expansion and Destruction in Gaza
gaza-territorial-control-2026.summary: Israel's systematic expansion of territorial control in Gaza beyond the October 2025 ceasefire Yellow Line, combined with near-total destruction of civilian infrastructure. Netanyahu directed the IDF to expand control from 60 to 70 percent of Gaza. Satellite imagery from February 2026 shows 94 percent of cemeteries destroyed, 97 percent of schools damaged or destroyed, and less than 5 percent of agricultural land usable. By June 2026, the post-ceasefire killing toll reached 1,007 Palestinians. US-appointed mediator Mladenov warned the Security Council the situation risks becoming 'permanent.'

west-bank-crackdown-2026.title: West Bank Military Crackdown and Settler Violence Surge (2026)
west-bank-crackdown-2026.summary: A wide-scale Israeli military operation across West Bank villages, ordered by Netanyahu and Defense Minister Katz on 24 July 2026 following an attack near Havat Gilad that killed two Israeli soldiers, and a separate deadly confrontation in the village of Tal that killed four Palestinians. The operation produced mass arrests, home raids across multiple governorates, and continued settler arson attacks, drawing condemnation from the UN Special Rapporteur on the Palestinian territories and Human Rights Watch.

saudi-israel-normalization-2026.title: US-Saudi Nuclear Deal and Abraham Accords Linkage (2026)
saudi-israel-normalization-2026.summary: Trump conditioned a newly announced US-Saudi civilian nuclear cooperation agreement on Saudi Arabia normalizing relations with Israel through the Abraham Accords, unsettling a deal unveiled a day earlier and reviving questions about uranium enrichment rights in the region.

entries.headline: Trump says Saudi nuclear deal 'totally subject' to Riyadh normalizing relations with Israel

hamas-leadership-transition-2026.title: Hamas Leadership Transition Under Khalil al-Hayya (2026)
hamas-leadership-transition-2026.summary: Khalil al-Hayya's election as Hamas's new political bureau chief and his first public address, in which he restated the group's existing positions on Gaza reconstruction, prisoner releases, and Palestinian statehood while pressing for enforcement of the October 2025 ceasefire.

entries.headline: New Hamas leader al-Hayya pledges to rebuild Gaza and unite Palestinian territories in first address

us-politicians-west-bank-2026.title: US Officials Confront West Bank Settler Impunity (2026)
us-politicians-west-bank-2026.summary: Incidents in which US officials visiting the West Bank have been obstructed or detained by Israeli settlers and soldiers, beginning with Representative Ro Khanna's detention on 8 July 2026, highlighting disputes over settler accountability and Israeli government responses to American criticism.

india-israel-arms-transfers-2026.title: India's Arms Pipeline to Israel During the Gaza War (2026)
india-israel-arms-transfers-2026.summary: Documentation, via Amnesty International and Al Jazeera investigations, of the scale of Indian state-owned and private-company arms shipments to Israel during the Gaza war, and the accountability questions this raises under international law.

entries.headline: Amnesty: India sent nearly 2,600 arms shipments to Israel during Gaza war

gaza-disarmament-roadmap-2026.title: Gaza Disarmament and Ceasefire Roadmap Negotiations (2026)
gaza-disarmament-roadmap-2026.summary: Negotiations brokered by the US-led Board of Peace with Egypt, Qatar and Turkiye over a phased roadmap requiring Hamas to disarm in stages as Israel withdraws its forces from Gaza -- the long-delayed next phase of the October 2025 ceasefire, announced 31 July 2026 amid rejection from Israeli hardliners and unresolved implementation questions.

entries.headline: Hamas agrees to phased Gaza disarmament roadmap as Israeli hardliners reject deal

us-palestine-solidarity-suppression-2026.title: US Crackdowns on Pro-Palestine Speech and Assembly (2026)
us-palestine-solidarity-suppression-2026.summary: Instances of US institutions -- venues, universities, state and local officials -- moving to cancel, restrict, or delegitimize pro-Palestinian or Israel-critical speech and assembly, often under accusations of antisemitism, illustrating a domestic front in the broader suppression of Palestine-related discourse.
